payload.purpose_context: Spec Kitty ships a set of built-in agent profiles (Debugger Debbie, Java Jenny, Python Pedro, Node Norris) that give missions stack-specific expertise. Drupal work currently has no such persona, so Drupal-specific conventions, module structure, and community practice are not represented in routing or governance. This mission adds 'Drupal Dries' as a first-class built-in profile, seeded from a community AGENTS.md for Drupal plus whatever the existing profile contract requires.
payload.purpose_tldr: Add a built-in Drupal-specialist agent profile so Spec Kitty missions can route Drupal work to an expert persona.

payload.question: Where is the Drupal AGENTS.md you found, and how should its content be used — verbatim seed, distilled into the profile contract, or reference only?

payload.final_answer: Source: https://github.com/amazeeio/drupal-agents-md/blob/main/Vanilla/AGENTS.md (amazee.io drupal-agents-md, Vanilla variant). Usage mode: B — distilled. Mine it for Drupal domain facts and re-express them in the existing built-in agent-profile YAML contract; do not copy verbatim.

payload.question: Which artifact package should this mission deliver: profile only, profile + conventions styleguide, or the full specialist package matching Java/Python (profile + styleguide + review-checks toolguide + anti-patterns)?
What roles does Dries hold — implementer only (like Java Jenny), or implementer plus reviewer/debugger breadth?

payload.final_answer: full-specialist-package: profile YAML + DRG nodes/edges + drupal-conventions styleguide + DRUPAL_REVIEW_CHECKS toolguide + Drupal anti-patterns, matching the Java Jenny / Python Pedro package shape.
implementer-only: roles [implementer], specializes_from implementer-ivan, hands off to reviewer-renata — same shape as Java Jenny and Python Pedro.

payload.question: Does Dries cover Drupal backend only, or also Drupal theming/frontend (Twig, libraries, JS behaviors)?
Which local environment should the self-review commands assume: vanilla host tooling (php/composer/drush directly), containerized (ddev/lando prefixes), or environment-agnostic?

payload.final_answer: backend-plus-theming: Dries covers Drupal backend (modules, DI/services, Entity API, plugins, hooks, Forms API, routing, config, Batch/Queue/Migration) AND Drupal theming (Twig, *.libraries.yml, Drupal.behaviors, render arrays, preprocess). Overlap with frontend-freddy must be resolved by an explicit boundary: Dries owns Drupal-native theming layer; generic SPA/framework frontend work stays with Freddy.
environment-agnostic: self-review commands written as bare composer/drush/phpcs/phpunit with an explicit note that containerized setups (ddev/lando) prefix them.

payload.question: Should Drupal conventions be one styleguide artifact (~400+ lines, well above the 158-170 line peer norm) or split into conventions plus a separate security/performance guide?
Does Dries's self-review gate include the JavaScript test commands (npm run test / test:a11y) for Drupal theming JS, or stop at the PHP gates and hand JS verification to Freddy?

payload.final_answer: split-conventions-and-security: two styleguide artifacts — drupal-conventions (style, DI, entity/plugin/hook/form/routing patterns, theming, 14 anti-patterns) and drupal-security-performance (sanitization, access checks, cacheability, query discipline). Each targets the 150-200 line peer norm.

include-js-gates: Dries's self-review protocol includes npm run test and npm run test:a11y in addition to the PHP gates. Boundary refinement required — verification scope is not authorship scope: Dries verifies the Drupal-native theming JS it authored; generic browser component work remains Freddy's to author. FR-004's boundary text must state this distinction explicitly.

review.reference: Review passed. Independently re-ran all four implementer claims; none taken on trust. (3) regenerate-graph --check exits 0 and prints the LANE WORKTREE's own packs/built-in, not a pipx path (R-003 trap avoided). (4) doctor doctrine --json profile_health = 25 discovered / 25 valid / 0 skipped / healthy=true. ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy all clean on the three files and on tests/doctrine/ as a whole. T004 negative case (FR-013) uses a tmp_path fixture, never the shipped pack, is mutation-verified sensitive (drop the malformed file and skipped==[], so len(skipped)==1 is load-bearing), and consumes the real production seam build_pack_health_by_layer. T005 asserts endpoint form <kind>:<id> explicitly via a regex that genuinely rejects urn:profile:... plus a NodeKind-member comparison, and uses a real 3-color DFS cycle detector rather than a single-hop shortcut. T006 carries no frozen literal: it reuses _builtin_inventory PACK_ROOT/FILE_BACKED_NODE_GLOBS and its glob-derived helper is proven correct by the fs-vs-graph equality test passing today. Scope clean: exactly the 3 owned_files, zero src/ or packs/ changes, shipped pack unmutated. --force used because the lane-hygiene gate fires on pre-existing tool-authored kitty-specs divergence (lane cut from a base predating the tasks commit; all such commits are spec-kitty status/scaffold/merge bookkeeping, none from the implementer). (b) test_doctor_doctrine_reports_zero_skipped_profiles never invokes the CLI, only repo.skipped_profiles(). (c) the negative case covers a YAML parse failure but not a schema-invalid profile. (d) _shipped_ids duplicates _builtin_inventory.builtin_profile_ids -- fold upstream once that file is in scope.

review.reference: Review passed (independent reviewer). Verified by running, not reading: T030 agreement script green in BOTH directions (guide_path exists: True; all 9 descriptor commands present VERBATIM in body, missing=[]; every body-fenced command either in the descriptor or a flag variant of vendor/bin/phpunit, matching the maven peer precedent 'mvn verify' vs 'mvn verify -Pcoverage'). C-S6: grep for '%', for a digit adjacent to 'level', and for coverage/mutation/threshold returns ZERO hits on both files; the only digits in the body are 'a11y' and 'DIRECTIVE_051'. Confirmed against the upstream source (amazeeio/drupal-agents-md Vanilla/AGENTS.md) that it names NO PHPStan level and DOES say 'Aim for >= 80% code coverage' - the implementer correctly declined to carry that threshold, and the substitute phrasing ('clean at the project's configured level ... this guide does not assert one', phpstan.neon) is honest, not weasel. C-S5: exactly one Environment note (single '## Environment' section); no command dual-listed. R-006: JS caveat states plainly that npm run test / test:a11y verify the Drupal-native theming JavaScript (Drupal.behaviors, *.libraries.yml assets) the implementer authored and that generic browser-component authorship remains Frontend Freddy's; no-package.json case handled. PHPUnit tiers teach SELECTION, not just invocation, with the canonical heavily-mocked-unit-test failure mode named explicitly. Drupal correctness spot-checked against upstream sources: DrupalPractice sniff tree fetched live from git.drupalcode.org confirms the Drupal-vs-DrupalPractice split AND the specific 'missing access checks' claim (RoutingAccessSniff, AccessAdminPagesSniff, AccessHookMenuSniff) and the \Drupal:: claim (GlobalDrupalSniff/GlobalClassSniff); drupal-check confirmed as the deprecation scanner; the three tier capabilities confirmed against drupal.org 'Types of tests'. All 9 commands trace to the source's Code Quality Tools / Before Submitting Code / Testing sections.
